cards.title: Engineering Acceleration, Not Superintelligence: A Grounded Take on Near-Term AI Progress
cards.why_it_matters: This is a detailed, technically grounded framework from an industry-connected observer on what AI-assisted research actually accelerates and what it doesn't — directly relevant to how you should think about your own work changing over the next few years.
cards.summary: The author argues near-term AI progress is best understood as parallelized, AI-assisted language modeling — not recursive self-improvement toward AGI. Inference efficiency gains (historically 10–30% cost reductions post-launch) will compound near-exponentially. Architecture and data-selection research may be largely automated in 2–3 years. The bottleneck shifts from engineering back to ideas, mirroring pre-deep-learning AI. Jevons paradox will drive demand higher as costs fall.

cards.title: Ai2 Replaces Priority Scheduler with Budget-Based Fair-Share System for H100/B200/B300 Clusters
cards.why_it_matters: If you work on or adjacent to ML infrastructure, this is a rare detailed post-mortem on GPU cluster scheduling pathologies and the architectural fix — directly applicable to any multi-team research compute environment.
cards.summary: Ai2's AI Infrastructure team manages clusters of 88–1024 NVIDIA H100, B200, and B300 GPUs serving ~150 researchers, with 2–3x more demand than supply at any moment. A priority-based scheduler produced GPU squatting, 100% priority inflation, and engineers spending most ticket time negotiating non-preemptable shutdowns. They replaced it with GPU time budgets, hierarchical fair-share allocation, and a time-slicing contract, moving resource debates from ad-hoc negotiation to transparent administrative budgeting.
